Snyk.author: guypod
Snyk.text: (I'm the founder of Snyk and Tessl, apply what biases you wish)I think we're mixing three optimizations: higher success rate, higher consistency and higher efficiency.Success rate is about building confidence the agent can succeed. The hardest part here is defining what success is in the first place, and creating evals that help you measure it. Consistency is about guardrails. The harness shines here, as it takes control away from the model, moving it to hooks that force certain paths, or require the use of deterministic tools for certain steps. Given consistency and success rate, you can work on efficiency. You can save cognition (tokens) by moving work to tools, try to use a cheaper model, etc.These three build on one another, at least if you want to scale them. You can't improve consistency if you don't define success, and you can't add efficiency if you're not consistent.

It's built on top of .HAR, an open-harness to run fleets of agents securely.Chatting with CTO/VP of Engineering from startups to F100, the challenges of factory build out are the same (just different scales):1. How do I ensure agents are not shipping things that break compliance, policies and features, without chewing up more and more senior engineering hours... it's not just bugs, it's the entire business chain..2. 84% of devs use AI. 3% trust it.... how do I scale trust/governance, so my junior devs act as a responsibly as my senior .. [or just automate this into the agent workflow]3.
